title: Common Phrasal Verbs list 4
intro: Learn the most common phrasal verbs in English with the following list.

meanings: When you collide with something by accident.
items.example: The car ran into a tree.

meanings: To make copies; to print
To suddenly leave without permission or to flee.
items.example: The dog ran off with my shoe.

meanings: When you do not have resources anymore.
items.example: We've run out of milk.

meanings: To review or rehearse something again.
items.example: Let's run through the plan once more.

meanings: When an amount reaches a certain cost.
items.example: The bill ran to 500 dollars.

items.es: darse cuenta de las intenciones de, no dejarse engañar por
meanings: To perceive something physically.
To recognize the true intentions of someone or something.
items.example: I can see through your lies.

meanings: To show something to impress people
items.example: He's always showing off his new car.

items.es: quedarse a dormir (en casa de alguien)
meanings: When you spend the night at someone else’s house, usually with friends.
items.example: Can my friend sleep over tonight?

meanings: To resemble someone because of similar characteristics.
items.example: She takes after her mother.

meanings: To remove something.
items.example: The waiter took away our plates.

meanings: To retract something you said.
To reclaim something that belong to you.
items.example: I'm sorry: I take back what I said.

meanings: To write something down in a piece of paper.
To dismantle an object.
items.example: Take down my phone number.

meanings: To finally understand something.
To provide lodging for someone or something.
items.example: It was too much information to take in.

meanings: To become successful.
To depart or leave.
items.example: The plane took off on time.

items.en: To take off something / to take something off
meanings: To remove clothing, accessories or objects.
items.example: Please take your shoes off at the door.

items.es: hacerse cargo de; tomar el control
meanings: To assume the responsibility of something.
To have control over something.
items.example: She took over the company in 2020.

meanings: To separate the components of objects.
items.example: He took the old radio apart.

meanings: To start a new hobby or something that attracts you.
To occupy space.
To use a lot of time.
items.example: I took up yoga last year.

items.en: To try out something / to try something out
meanings: To test something to see if it works.
items.example: Let's try out the new restaurant.

meanings: To consume everything provided by something.
items.example: Who used up all the hot water?

meanings: To eliminate something forever.
items.example: The storm wiped out the whole village.

meanings: When you exercise.
When you try to find a solution for something.
items.example: I work out at the gym three times a week.
